title: Docker
subtitle: Build, ship and run applications as isolated, reproducible containers.

tiles.label: Image layers
tiles.says: Images are stacked, read-only, content-addressed layers.
tiles.detail: Shared layers save disk and bandwidth, and caching makes builds fast.

tiles.label: Dockerfile
tiles.says: A Dockerfile declares how an image is built.
tiles.detail: Reproducible, reviewable builds replace manual server setup. Multi-stage builds ship small images.

tiles.label: Registries
tiles.detail: Pull by digest guarantees identical artifacts across environments, which is the basis of reliable releases.

tiles.label: Engine
tiles.says: The Docker engine manages images, networks and volumes.
tiles.detail: It translates simple commands into containerd operations and exposes an API for tooling.

tiles.label: containerd
tiles.says: containerd supervises container lifecycle and snapshots.
tiles.detail: A stable, CRI-compatible runtime also used directly by Kubernetes.

tiles.label: runc
tiles.says: runc creates the container process from an OCI spec.
tiles.detail: It applies namespaces and cgroups then starts the entrypoint.

tiles.label: Namespaces
tiles.says: Namespaces give each container its own view of the system.
tiles.detail: PID, network, mount, UTS and IPC isolation make processes unaware of neighbours.

tiles.label: Cgroups
tiles.says: Cgroups cap CPU, memory and I/O.
tiles.detail: Limits prevent one container from starving the host, so density rises safely.

tiles.label: Bridge networks
tiles.says: veth pairs attach containers to a virtual bridge.
tiles.detail: NAT and published ports connect containers to the outside, with user-defined networks adding DNS.

declarations: Containers are processes, not virtual machines.
Images are immutable; containers are disposable.
